answer: A reputation bond works like an opal that only gains its shine after slow, verifiable work: each agent must lock a refundable stake and build a history of useful tasks before it can transact at full trust. A newcomer that behaves like a passing comet — appearing, spamming, then vanishing — never accumulates enough history to matter, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities costs a thousand stakes and a thousand wasted histories, while honest agents keep one durable identity. Even a walnut-hard shell of encryption around an identity cannot fake that history.
